title: Quarterly sprint architectonics for Hosted API + Model Catalog
creator: Marina Koh
description:
Objective: Define a repeatable quarterly "architectonics" (structured sprint architecture) that maps Hosted API endpoint changes and model catalog rotations into scenario-driven execution lanes. This ticket synthesizes planning artifacts, creates a prioritized milestone slate, and produces the deliverables PM/Eng/Design need to run 8-week cycles with clear rollback, capacity, and eval gates.

Rationale: We have a high cadence of model updates and endpoint features; ad-hoc planning increases review overhead and operational risk. This work creates a compact, scenario-first roadmap representation so stakeholders can reason about commit windows, canaries, and capacity hedges for each quarter.

Deliverables:
- Quarterly Architectonics doc (this ticket) with scenario lanes and acceptance gates.
- Milestone calendar with canary windows and staffing signals.
- Release matrix tying each host endpoint to model tier, fallback variant, and latency hedges.
- Evaluation checklist (regression prompts, SLO smoke tests, sample telemetry queries).
- Dashboards templates (Console) for launch and post-launch monitoring.

Success metrics:
- 75% of planned model rotations have automated canaries and rollback within retained commit window for Q2.
- Mean time to detect* regressions <= 30m for hosted endpoints after rollout.
- Reduction in cross-team review cycles by 30% compared to previous quarter.
acceptance_criteria: Scenario lanes defined for Low/Medium/High risk changes with explicit gating and owner for each lane.
For each scheduled model swap, we list: model variant, canary fraction, fallback variant, capacity hedge, and eval-set link.
Ops runbook and Console dashboard template created and reviewed by Reliability (ENG) and SRE leads.
PM + Eng + Design sign-off on milestone calendar and staffing rotations for canary windows.
Post-launch regression checklist and smoke-test queries added to runtime-1.20 staging runbook.

stakeholders: Riley Thompson (SRE) - stability and on-call coordination
decisions: Adopt three scenario lanes: conservative (low-risk), iterative (medium-risk), experimental (high-risk).
Canary policy: default 5% for low-risk model swaps, 15% for iterative, 2% for experimental with manual gate.
Fallback policy: always keep a CPU/quantized-compatible variant pinned for each hosted endpoint.
Rollouts will require an automated smoke test within 10 minutes of canary traffic initiation.
risks: Model regressions that evade eval sets -> mitigated by expanding regression prompt suite and adding human spot checks for high-impact endpoints.
Capacity mismatch during simultaneous canaries -> hedging via reserved burst pools in Dedicated for peak windows.
Cross-team staffing gaps during canary windows -> implement a lightweight on-call rota for PM/design/eng owners.
rollout_plan: Pre-launch: confirm eval-set health, update Console dashboard, run smoke tests in staging.
Canary launch: open canary fraction, monitor user-facing errors and token latency heatmap for 30m.
Decision gate: if any SLO breach or regression signal present, pause + rollback to pinned fallback variant.
Full rollout: incremental increase in 2x steps with 1h stabilization checks between steps.
